pages.text: A table changed everything, and nothing. I could make tools of wood and stone, but stone only goes so deep. Metal was the next promise, and metal wanted fire hotter than any campfire.
I found clay in the shallows of a river and built a bloomery: clay and stone stacked around a hungry fire. I fed it logs until they blackened into charcoal, and then I fed it ore.
Copper alone is soft. Tin alone is brittle. Together they become bronze, and bronze holds an edge. I think about that often. Most things in this world are like that.
By the time I had forged five tools, I had a farm, a kitchen and neighbours: settlers who came when they saw bronze, like moths to a lantern. A colony grows where there is metal.
Copper and tin, fire and patience. One day a block of it will sit beside everything that came after.
pages.title: Mark of the Bronze Age
